BiblicalUsage: Nasag means to retreat or to move a boundary back, and it is used for landmarks and for borders. In Deuteronomy 19:14 no one shall remove his neighbour's landmark, which they of old time set in the inheritance, and in Hosea 5:10 the princes of Judah are like those who remove the bound, so the Lord pours out His wrath on them like water.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a moved landmark is a quiet theft, because nobody sees the fence walk a few feet in the night; God sees it, and Hosea says His wrath follows it like water.
